q: `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` meets a row that already exists. What happens?
options: The new row is skipped, with no error (the result says INSERT 0 0)
An error is raised
The old row is deleted
Both rows are saved
why: DO NOTHING skips the row. DO UPDATE changes the old row.

q: What does ON CONFLICT need in order to work?
options: A foreign key
A unique rule (a unique index or constraint) on the columns
A transaction at SERIALIZABLE level
An ORDER BY
why: Without a unique rule, the database cannot know what a conflict is.

q: Your code does: SELECT to check if the event exists, then INSERT if not. Two requests run at the same moment. What can happen?
options: Postgres puts them in a line, so it is safe
One request gets an error from SELECT
Both see 'not found' and both insert, so there is a duplicate
The second INSERT is ignored automatically
why: The database must enforce 'only one'. A unique rule stops the duplicate. ON CONFLICT makes the loser quiet.

q: You process a payment webhook that may arrive twice. How do you make it safe?
options: Add a sleep before handling it
Remember the event id in a variable in memory
Ask the sender not to send it twice
Save the event id with a unique rule, in the same transaction as the work. The unique id decides who goes first
why: That is an idempotency key. Assume every event, request and job can arrive twice.

q: Several workers take jobs with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 1`. What does SKIP LOCKED do?
options: A worker skips jobs that another worker has locked, and takes the next one instead of waiting
It deletes locked jobs
It makes all workers take the same job
It stops the queue until the lock is free
why: FOR UPDATE makes the job yours. SKIP LOCKED makes the others look at the next job.

q: A worker dies in the middle of a job. What happens to the job in a database queue?
options: The job is lost for ever
Its transaction is rolled back and the job goes back to pending, so the work must be safe to run twice
The job is marked done
The database restarts the worker
why: Make the work safe to run twice, because it may run again.
